stories.title: Optimus Prime and Eeyore voice actor Peter Cullen dies
stories.summary: Actor Peter Cullen, who voiced popular characters including Optimus Prime in Transformers and Eeyore in Disney's Winnie the Pooh franchise, has died at the age of 85. The Canadian actor began his most famous role - as the heroic deep-voiced Optimus Prime - for the Transformers TV series in 1984, then returned for seven Hollywood films from 2007 to 2023 and other spin-offs. He voiced depressive donkey Eeyore in TV animation. The New Adventures of Winnie the Pooh from the late 1980s as well as numerous related shows, films and games. His other memorable voice parts included KARR, the evil counterpart to KITT in TV show Knight Rider; the clicking vocalisations of The Predator in Arnold Schwarzenegger's 1987 film; and the roars of King Kong in 1976. He died on Wednesday at his home in Los Angeles, a statement said. "Peter Cullen passed away peacefully, surrounded by his loving family - and held in the hearts of his many friends and countless fans worldwide. "His family asks that you honour his remarkable legacy by serving your communities and leading others with compassion, integrity, and loyalty and always remember 'be strong enough to be gentle'." Cullen started his career on Canadian TV and radio and was then a regular on programmes like. The Sonny & Cher Show before deciding to concentrate on voice acting. His Optimus Prime voice was inspired by his older brother, a decorated US Marine and Vietnam War veteran, who suggested he should play the character as "a real hero, don't be a Hollywood hero". "He said, 'Don't go yelling and screaming.

stories.title: Qatar PM meets Iran’s Araghchi in Tehran as Doha pushes de-escalation and reopening Hormuz
stories.summary: Qatar is stepping up its mediation efforts as regional tensions remain high and direct US-Iran talks remain stalled, with Doha focused on de-escalation, dialogue and restoring freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani visited Tehran on Thursday as Doha stepped up efforts to revive diplomacy and ease tensions around the Strait of Hormuz. Sheikh Mohammed, who also serves as Qatar’s foreign minister, held talks with Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in the first high-level Qatari visit to Tehran since the war began on 28 February. The talks focused on efforts to reduce tensions and create conditions for renewed dialogue between Iran and the US, according to Qatar’s state news agency QNA. The two officials also discussed ongoing talks on a proposed phased plan for the Strait of Hormuz, including a temporary shipping corridor and a joint project to clear mines from the waterway. Sheikh Mohammed stressed the need to respect the sovereignty of neighbouring countries and freedom of navigation, and called for diplomatic efforts to continue resolving differences through dialogue. Araghchi thanked Qatar for its mediation efforts and continued support for dialogue. The visit comes nearly six months into the war, with direct fighting largely paused but no diplomatic breakthrough in sight. Qatar, a US ally that hosts the US military’s Al Udeid Air Base and shares the world’s largest gas field with Iran, has played a key role as a mediator between Washington and Tehran and helped broker the June ceasefire that briefly halted the fighting. The war and disruption to shipping have come at a high cost. Industry data show Qatar exported just 18 LNG cargoes over the past six months, compared with 509 in the same period a year earlier. Before the war, Qatar supplied about one-fifth of global LNG.

stories.title: Pakistan: Protests continue in Azad Kashmir despite repression and internet blackout
stories.summary: Harshly repressed protests that have shaken Pakistan-administered Kashmir since early June have continued through local legislative elections held in July and August. With internet access cut off and access by foreign media restricted, local residents are attempting to report on the situation on the ground.
